'''Philippe Lehert'''  (born August 1, 1949) is a Belgian [[scientist]] specializing in [[mathematical statistics]] and biostatistics.

== Early life and education ==
Lehert earned a [[Master of Science]] in [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] and Engineering from the Faculty of Applied Mathematics in Mons, Belgium, in 1974. He later completed his PhD at the Department of Mathematics of Mons University, focusing on computational complexity in [[cluster analysis]] within Euclidean spaces.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philippe Lehert |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=O3WugqoAAAAJ&hl=fr |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

== Achievements ==
Lehert is an Honorary Professor at the School of Management, Louvain University, Belgium, and the Faculty of Medicine at the [[University of Melbourne]], Australia. He has also served as a statistical adviser for the United Nations and a member of the Belgian Board of Statistics.{{Citation needed|date=February 2025}}

In the field of pattern recognition and [[artificial intelligence]], he provided the first demonstration of the linear expected time O(n) complexity of clustering by connected components for any Minkowsky distances, based on cubic tessellations structures in hyperspaces.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1992 |title=Classification en composantes connexes, cas particulier de l'ultramétrique inférieure maximale: un algorithme O(n) en temps moyen |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/RSA_1992__40_3_63_0.pdf |website=Numdam}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 1995 |title=Critical percolation properties to prove existence of O(n) expected time single linkage clustering algorithm at a predetermined threshold |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268615209 |website=ResearchGate}}</ref>
